subject: Biology
summary: Covers classical Mendelian genetics, 7 Pisum sativum traits, Monohybrid and Dihybrid cross mechanics, Test cross, Incomplete dominance (Antirrhinum), Co-dominance & Multiple alleles (ABO blood groups), Pleiotropy & Polygenic inheritance, Sutton-Boveri Chromosome Theory, Morgan's Drosophila experiments, Linkage and Sturtevant's genetic mapping, Sex determination systems across taxa (including honeybee haplodiploidy), Pedigree analysis, Mendelian monogenic disorders (Sickle-cell, Thalassemia, PKU, Hemophilia), and Chromosomal aneuploidies (Down, Turner, Klinefelter syndromes).

sections.title: Mendel's Principles, Seven Traits, & Monohybrid Cross
sections.topic: Mendelian Hybridization, Pisum sativum 7 Contrasting Characters, & Law of Segregation

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Gregor Mendel (1856–1863) analyzed 7 contrasting traits on Chromosomes 1, 4, 5, 7 in Pisum sativum. Law of Dominance and Law of Segregation (Universal - purity of gametes). Monohybrid cross yields F2 phenotypic ratio 3:1 and genotypic ratio 1:2:1.

sections.codeSnippet:
MENDEL'S EXPERIMENTAL ADVANTAGES
                                         │
         ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                               ▼                               ▼
  SEVEN CONSTRASTING TRAITS      BISEXUAL / SELF-POLLINATING     SHORT LIFE CYCLE
  Clear-cut qualitative          Easy to self-fertilize or       Yields large number of
  either-or characters.          artificially cross-pollinate.   offspring per generation.
sections.content:
### 1.1 Mendel's Principles of Inheritance
- **Mendel's Pea Traits**: 7 pairs on chromosomes 1, 4, 5, and 7.
- **Law of Segregation**: Alleles segregate cleanly during meiosis; universal with zero exceptions.
- **Monohybrid Cross**: $TT \times tt \rightarrow F_1: Tt \rightarrow F_2: 3:1$ phenotypic ratio, $1:2:1$ genotypic ratio.

sections.title: Dihybrid Cross & Test Cross Mechanics
sections.topic: Law of Independent Assortment, Dihybrid 9:3:3:1, & Test Cross 1:1 and 1:1:1:1

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Dihybrid Cross (RRYY × rryy) yields F2 phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1 with 9 distinct genotypes (1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1). Test cross crosses dominant phenotype with homozygous recessive parent (Monohybrid test cross = 1:1; Dihybrid test cross = 1:1:1:1).

sections.codeSnippet:
TEST CROSS ARCHITECTURE
                            
      Homozygous Dominant (TT x tt)          Heterozygous Dominant (Tt x tt)
            t       t                                     t       t
        T  Tt      Tt                                 T  Tt      Tt
        T  Tt      Tt                                 t  tt      tt
      Ratio: 100% Dominant                          Ratio: 1:1 Dominant : Recessive
sections.content:
### 2.1 Dihybrid Cross & Test Cross
- **Dihybrid F2 Ratios**: $9:3:3:1$ phenotypic, $1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1$ genotypic.
- **Test Cross**: Used to identify unknown dominant genotypes ($T\_ \times tt$).

sections.title: Incomplete Dominance & Co-Dominance Genetics
sections.topic: Antirrhinum majus 1:2:1 Ratio, Co-dominance, & Allelic Expression

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Incomplete dominance (Antirrhinum majus): F1 pink flowers, F2 phenotypic ratio equals genotypic ratio (1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White = 1:2:1). Co-dominance: both alleles express equally in heterozygote.

sections.codeSnippet:
EXTENSIONS TO MENDELISM
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
INCOMPLETE DOMINANCE            CO-DOMINANCE                    MULTIPLE ALLELISM
F1 phenotype is intermediate    Both alleles express fully      >2 alleles govern a trait in
between parental extremes.      in the F1 heterozygote.         a population (ABO Blood).
├── Antirrhinum majus           ├── ABO Blood Group (IA IB)     ├── Population-level trait
└── Phenotypic Ratio: 1:2:1     └── Phenotypic Ratio: 1:2:1     └── Genotypes = n(n+1)/2
sections.content:
### 3.1 Non-Mendelian Extensions
- **Incomplete Dominance**: F2 phenotypic ratio ($1:2:1$) matches genotypic ratio.
- **Co-dominance**: Heterozygote expresses both alleles equally without intermediate blending.

sections.title: Multiple Allelism & ABO Blood Group Genetics
sections.topic: ABO Locus on Chromosome 9, Glycosyltransferase Enzymes, 6 Genotypes, & 4 Phenotypes

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: ABO blood group is controlled by the I gene on Chromosome 9 with 3 alleles (IA, IB, i). Total genotypes = n(n+1)/2 = 6 genotypes resulting in 4 phenotypes (A, B, AB, O).

sections.codeSnippet:
ABO GENETICS MATRIX
                           
   ALLELE      ENZYME PRODUCT                          DOMINANCE RELATIONSHIP
   I^A         N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase       Completely dominant over i; Co-dominant with I^B
   I^B         Galactosyltransferase                   Completely dominant over i; Co-dominant with I^A
   i           Non-functional enzyme (No sugar added)  Recessive to both I^A and I^B
sections.content:
### 4.1 Multiple Allelism
- **Formula**: $\text{Diploid Genotypes} = n(n+1)/2 = 6$.
- **ABO Phenotypes**: Group A ($I^A I^A, I^A i$), Group B ($I^B I^B, I^B i$), Group AB ($I^A I^B$), Group O ($ii$).

sections.title: Pleiotropy & Polygenic Quantitative Inheritance
sections.topic: Single Gene Multiple Phenotypes (PKU, Pea Starch) & Additive Polygenic Skin Color

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pleiotropy: one gene influences multiple phenotypic traits (PKU, pea starch Bb). Polygenic inheritance: multiple additive genes control a single continuous trait (human skin color: 1:6:15:20:15:6:1 across 64 combinations).

sections.codeSnippet:
PLEIOTROPY vs POLYGENIC INHERITANCE
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   PLEIOTROPY                                              POLYGENIC INHERITANCE
   ONE single gene influences MULTIPLE,                    MULTIPLE additive genes control
   apparently unrelated phenotypic traits.                 a SINGLE continuous trait.
   ├── Phenylketonuria (PKU)                               ├── Human Skin Color (A, B, C genes)
   └── Starch grain size vs seed shape in Peas             └── Wheat Kernel Color (1:4:6:4:1)
sections.content:
### 5.1 Pleiotropy & Polygenic Inheritance
- **Pleiotropy**: PKU (PAH mutation causes retardation and hypopigmentation); Pea starch $Bb$ gene.
- **Polygenic Inheritance**: Human skin color (3 additive gene pairs $A, B, C$ yielding Gaussian distribution).

sections.title: Chromosome Theory & Morgan's Drosophila Experiments
sections.topic: Sutton-Boveri Chromosome Theory & Drosophila Melanogaster Experimental Advantages

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Sutton and Boveri (1902) proposed Chromosome Theory of Inheritance. T.H. Morgan experimentally proved the theory using Drosophila melanogaster (2-week life cycle, 2n=8, clear sexual dimorphism).

sections.codeSnippet:
GENE vs CHROMOSOME BEHAVIOR PARALLELISM
                      
   GENES (Mendelian Factors)                   CHROMOSOMES (Cytological Units)
   ├── Occur in pairs in diploid cells         ├── Occur in homologous pairs in diploid cells
   ├── Segregate at gamete formation (1/2)     ├── Homologs segregate at Anaphase I (1/2)
   └── Independent assortment of gene pairs    └── Independent alignment at Metaphase I
sections.content:
### 6.1 Chromosome Theory of Inheritance
- **Parallelism**: Sutton-Boveri parallel behavior of genes and chromosomes.
- **Morgan's Drosophila**: 2-week life cycle, high fecundity, clear sexual dimorphism, $2n=8$.

sections.title: Linkage, Crossing Over, & Genetic Mapping
sections.topic: Morgan's Crosses I & II, Recombination Frequency, & Sturtevant's cM Gene Mapping

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Linkage is co-inheritance of genes on same chromosome. Morgan Cross I (y & w): 98.7% parental, 1.3% recombinant (tight linkage). Cross II (w & m): 62.8% parental, 37.2% recombinant (loose linkage). Sturtevant: 1% RF = 1 cM. Max RF = 50%.

sections.codeSnippet:
LINKAGE vs RECOMBINATION
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   TIGHT LINKAGE                                           LOOSE LINKAGE
   Genes positioned close together.                        Genes positioned far apart.
   ├── High Parental Phenotypes (~99%)                     ├── Higher Recombinants (up to 50%)
   └── Low Recombinants (Morgan's Cross I: 1.3%)           └── Morgan's Cross II: 37.2%
sections.content:
### 7.1 Linkage & Gene Mapping
- **Morgan's Crosses**: Cross I (y, w: $1.3\%$ RF); Cross II (w, m: $37.2\%$ RF).
- **Sturtevant's Map Unit**: $1\%\text{ Recombination Frequency} = 1\text{ cM}$. Maximum observable $\text{RF} = 50\%$.

sections.title: Sex Determination Systems & Honeybee Haplodiploidy
sections.topic: XX-XY, XX-XO, ZZ-ZW Systems, & Parthenogenetic Haploid Drones in Honeybees

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Sex determination: XX-XY (Humans/Drosophila), XX-XO (Grasshopper), ZZ-ZW (Birds). Haplodiploidy in honeybees: Queen 2n=32, Drones n=16 (develop by parthenogenesis and produce sperm by MITOSIS).

sections.codeSnippet:
SEX DETERMINATION SYSTEMS
                                       │
     ┌──────────────────┬──────────────┴──────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                             ▼                  ▼
  XX - XY SYSTEM     XX - XO SYSTEM                ZZ - ZW SYSTEM      HAPLODIPLOPIDY
  Male Heterogametic Male Heterogametic           Female Heterogametic Females 2n; Males n
  ├── Male: XY       ├── Male: XO (Henking X)     ├── Female: ZW       └── Parthenogenesis
  └── Female: XX     └── Female: XX               └── Male: ZZ             (Honeybees)
  (Humans, Drosophila)(Grasshoppers)              (Birds, Butterflies)
sections.content:
### 8.1 Sex Determination Systems
- **Male Heterogamety**: XX-XY (Humans, Drosophila), XX-XO (Grasshoppers).
- **Female Heterogamety**: ZZ-ZW (Birds, Butterflies).
- **Honeybee Haplodiploidy**: Drones are haploid ($n=16$) and produce sperm via mitosis.

sections.title: Human Pedigree Analysis & Pattern Recognition
sections.topic: Standard Pedigree Symbols & Autosomal vs X-Linked Inheritance Rules

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pedigree analysis: squares (males), circles (females), double lines (consanguineous mating). Autosomal Dominant (does not skip generations), Autosomal Recessive (skips generations), X-Linked Recessive (criss-cross inheritance, mostly males).

sections.codeSnippet:
PEDIGREE SYMBOLS
                         
   Square       ──► Normal Male               Filled Square  ──► Affected Male
   Circle       ──► Normal Female             Filled Circle  ──► Affected Female
   Diamond      ──► Sex Unspecified           Filled Diamond ──► Affected Unspecified
   Single Line  ──► Mating                    Double Line    ──► Consanguineous Mating (Relatives)
sections.content:
### 9.1 Pedigree Pattern Recognition
- **Autosomal Dominant**: Does not skip generations; equal male/female ratio.
- **Autosomal Recessive**: Skips generations; carrier parents produce affected offspring.
- **X-Linked Recessive**: Criss-cross inheritance; carrier mother passes to sons.

sections.title: Mendelian Monogenic Disorders & Chromosomal Aneuploidies
sections.topic: Sickle-Cell Anemia, Thalassemia, PKU, Hemophilia, Down, Turner, & Klinefelter Syndromes

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Sickle-Cell Anemia: GAG -> GUG Glu6Val point mutation. Thalassemia: quantitative globin defect. PKU: inborn PAH defect. Hemophilia & Color Blindness: X-linked recessive. Aneuploidies: Down's (47,+21), Turner's (45,X0 - 0 Barr bodies), Klinefelter's (47,XXY - 1 Barr body).

sections.codeSnippet:
SICKLE-CELL ANEMIA POINT MUTATION
                       
   Normal beta-Globin (HbA):   DNA: CTC ──► mRNA: GAG ──► Amino Acid: Glutamic Acid (Position 6)
   Sickle beta-Globin (HbS):   DNA: CAC ──► mRNA: GUG ──► Amino Acid: VALINE (Position 6)
sections.content:
### 10.1 Genetic Disorders Matrix
- **Sickle-Cell Anemia**: Autosomal recessive $\text{Glu}6\text{Val}$ transversion point mutation.
- **Thalassemia**: Quantitative globin chain deficiency.
- **Down's Syndrome**: Trisomy 21 ($47, XX/XY, +21$).
- **Turner's Syndrome**: Monosomy $45, X0$ (sterile female, 0 Barr bodies).
- **Klinefelter's Syndrome**: Trisomy $47, XXY$ (sterile male, gynecomastia, 1 Barr body).

sections.title: Genetics Glossary & High-Yield NEST Traps
sections.topic: Master Genetics Glossary & 10 High-Yield Exam Traps

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Master genetics glossary with 50+ definitions and 10 high-yield NEST misconceptions and numerical invariant traps.

sections.content:
### 11.1 Master Genetics Glossary & Traps
- **Independent Assortment Limit**: Applies only to unlinked genes.
- **Thalassemia vs Sickle-Cell**: Quantitative defect vs Qualitative defect.
- **Honeybee Drones**: Produce sperm by mitosis.
- **Barr Body Formula**: $\text{Barr Bodies} = \text{Total } X - 1$.
